# Harness Control Protocol (HCP)

> HCP lets a hosted app drive coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) on a user's own machine. A local runner (`@harness-control/runner`) connects out to the app's server (the control plane) over WebSocket. The app sends commands and receives events. There is no central HCP service: every app runs its own control plane.

Packages: `@harness-control/protocol` (types, Zod and JSON Schemas, event reducer), `@harness-control/sdk` (app side, TypeScript), `@harness-control/runner` (user's machine, plus `check-control-plane`). All three share one version.

## Rules an integration must follow

- The app owns pairing approval, sign-in, machine ownership, authorisation, the WebSocket server, and storage of commands, events and replay cursors. HCP owns the wire formats, the lifecycle spec and the checks.
- Pairing uses three HTTP endpoints at the control-plane origin: `POST /pairing-codes`, `POST /pairing-exchange`, `POST /runner-connection-token`. Bodies are in `@harness-control/protocol/pairing.schema.json`.
- The runner is given the WebSocket URL, for example `https://app.example.com/hcp/runner`. The exchange response's `control_plane_url` must equal that exact URL.
- Two steps must be atomic: consuming an approved pairing (once only), and spending a connection token (once only, while its credential generation is current).
- Revocation raises the credential generation, refuses new and previously minted tokens, and closes the live socket.
- Keep at most one live connection per credential. Check `host.hello`'s `runner_id` and `host_id` against the credential before `accept`.
- Pin `protocol_schema_sha256` to the protocol version you tested, and refuse others with HTTP 4xx.
- An ACK means accepted, not finished. A turn ends with `turn.completed`, `turn.failed`, `turn.aborted` or `turn.cancelled`. Start `waitForSessionEvent` before sending the command that causes the event.
- Store a command before sending it if you need crash recovery, and keep its id on retry. The SDK never retries. A timeout or disconnect means the outcome is unknown: reconcile with a snapshot before sending another change.
- Pass `accept` only a replay cursor you have durably stored. A missing capability means unknown, not removed.
- The runner's local policy wins. Never widen a requested sandbox or approval policy to make a provider work.
- Agent setup from the app (`setupProvider`) names only the agent and `install` or `update`. It works only for agents the machine's user listed in `provider_setup.remote_agents`; the runner picks the tested version. Sign-in is never automated: show `auth.login_command` to the user.
- Prove a control plane with `npx @harness-control/runner check-control-plane <runner-url> --hooks <test-hooks-url>`. It needs test-only `approve`, `decline` and `revoke` hooks.
